title: Vibecoding: what Claude Code is (and isn't) good for, and how non-coders use it
summary: Ruben argues vibecoding won't make you rich but is worth it for two things: clickable mockups to brief developers and small custom tools for yourself or your team. He gives a setup guide, a CTO-style mega prompt, taste tricks, cost habits, and a rule for when to hand the project to a real coder.

principles.text: Vibecoding is not a get-rich-quick path; its value is mockups for devs and small custom tools.
principles.quote: Getting rich or having a functioning company is far more complex than just knowing how to prompt an AI. I won’t sell you a get-rich-quick scam.

principles.text: Build a clickable version of your idea so developers and designers stop guessing what you meant.
principles.quote: you build a clickable version of your idea and hand it to someone, like a developer or a designer, so they stop guessing what you meant.

principles.text: Build small tools just for yourself or your team; rough edges are fine when nobody else sees them.
principles.quote: you build a small tool that does the job better than a simple Claude-chatbot interface. Just for you, your team, or a few customers. Rough edges are fine because nobody else sees them.

principles.text: Describe the end result and let the AI pick the steps, then build one piece at a time.
principles.quote: Say what you want to exist, and let Claude pick the steps.

principles.text: Avoid generic AI-looking sites by feeding specific references, screenshots and design system files.
principles.quote: The more specific you are, the less generic it looks.

principles.text: Don't spend longer building a tool than you'll spend using it; avoid performative productivity.
principles.quote: Do not take longer to build it than to consume it.
